items.title: Trump claims Iran in 'state of collapse,' wants Hormuz reopened

featured_image.name: Trump extends Iran ceasefire but continues Hormuz blockade

items.description:
President Donald Trump claimed on Tuesday that Iran has asked the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, portraying Tehran as desperate to end a naval blockade that has choked its economy amid a fragile ceasefire between the two nations.

"Iran has just informed us that they are in a 'State of Collapse.' They want us to 'Open the Hormuz Strait,' as soon as possible, as they try to figure out their leadership situation," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that he believes Iran will be able to resolve its internal issues.[1][2][3]

items.title: DOJ indicts former FBI director Comey a second time

featured_image.name: Federal judge sets back Justice Department's effort to seek new ...

items.description:
The Department of Justice has indicted former FBI Director James Comey for the second time, CNN reported on Tuesday, citing two sources familiar with the matter. The specific charges in the new indictment have not yet been publicly disclosed.

The move marks an escalation in the Trump administration's legal pursuit of Comey, whose first indictment in September 2025 was dismissed after a federal judge found the prosecutor who brought the case had been unlawfully appointed.

items.title: Japanese supertanker becomes first to exit Gulf since Iran war began

featured_image.name: 1st Japanese crude tanker crosses Hormuz since start of Mideast conflict

items.description: A sanctioned Russian oligarch's superyacht and a Japanese crude oil supertanker have each transited the blockaded Strait of Hormuz in recent days, underscoring cracks in the competing maritime restrictions imposed by the United States and Iran since war broke out in late February.

items.title: Study confirms deep-ocean heat is shifting toward Antarctica

featured_image.name: Trapped subsurface heat may have triggered Antarctica's sudden sea ice loss

items.description:
Warm water lurking deep in the Southern Ocean has been creeping steadily closer to Antarctica over the past two decades, eroding the cold barrier that has long shielded the continent's ice shelves from melting, according to a study published this week in the journal Communications Earth & Environment.[1]

The research, led by the University of Cambridge with collaborators from the Scripps Institution of Oceanography and UCLA, represents the first observational confirmation that a vast body of warm water known as circumpolar deep water has expanded and shifted toward the Antarctic continental shelf. Climate models had long predicted such a migration, but until now scientists lacked the data to confirm it was underway.[2][3]

items.title: Iran war reshapes global energy as renewables shield some nations from price surge

featured_image.name: A timeline of how the Iran war shook oil prices — and what comes next

items.description: The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran has triggered what the International Energy Agency calls the "greatest global energy security challenge in history," reshaping energy flows worldwide as extreme heat compounds the crisis. The disruption is driving record demand for Chinese clean energy exports, pushing fossil fuel-dependent nations like India to their limits, and offering a case study in resilience for renewable-heavy countries like Albania.

items.title: UCLA study finds desert dust traps twice the heat models estimated

featured_image.name: Climate change is altering Saharan dust – and Europe is downwind

items.description:
Airborne desert dust absorbs and retains roughly twice as much of Earth's heat as climate models have calculated, according to new research from UCLA published in Nature Communications.[1][2]

The study, led by UCLA atmospheric scientist Jasper Kok, found that the heat-trapping effect of dust is equal to about 10% of the warming caused by human-emitted carbon dioxide — double the approximately 5% that most climate models currently estimate.[2][1]

items.title: UAE exits OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, fracturing oil alliance

featured_image.name: Middle East Newsletter: Saudis, UAE End Dispute That Rocked OPEC

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates announced on Tuesday that it is withdrawing from both OPEC and OPEC+, effective May 1, dealing a severe blow to the oil-producing alliance and its de facto leader, Saudi Arabia, at a time when the Iran war has already caused the largest supply disruption in the history of global oil markets.[1][2]

The departure of the UAE — a founding member of OPEC since 1967, four years before the nation's own founding — marks the most consequential defection from the cartel in decades and could weaken an organization that has long sought to project unity despite internal rifts over production quotas and geopolitics.[2][1]

items.title: Osaka researchers demo wireless EEG powered by body heat alone

featured_image.name: No batteries, just body heat: Demonstrating the potential of battery-free  sensing

items.description: Researchers at the University of Osaka have developed a wireless brainwave monitoring system that runs entirely on the temperature difference between the human body and surrounding air, eliminating the need for batteries or any external power source. The work, published in the Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, was demonstrated live at Expo 2025 in Osaka, Japan.[1][2]

items.title: OpenAI misses revenue and user targets ahead of IPO

featured_image.name: OpenAI resets spend expectations, targets around $600 billion by ...

items.description: OpenAI has fallen short of internal revenue and user acquisition goals in 2026, according to a Wall Street Journal report published Monday, intensifying questions about whether the artificial intelligence company can sustain its enormous infrastructure spending as it prepares for a planned initial public offering later this year.[1][2]

items.title: Over 23,000 Iranian businesses destroyed as war's economic toll mounts

featured_image.name: IDF: It will take Iran years to rebuild its military industrial complex

items.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched a military campaign against Iran on February 28, the scale of destruction to the country's industrial base is coming into sharp focus. More than 23,000 factories and businesses have been damaged or destroyed, according to reports from Iranian media cited by CNN, leaving millions of workers without income and sending inflation to 72% as of March.[1][2]

items.title: CATL shares drop after $5 billion Hong Kong placement

featured_image.name: CATL shares slide after $5 billion Hong Kong share placement plan

items.description: Shares of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd., the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, fell more than 8% on Tuesday after the company announced a $5 billion share placement in Hong Kong — the city's largest equity offering this year.

items.title: Longi tops Trina Solar with 28.13% silicon solar cell record

featured_image.name: Trinasolar Sets New n-type Solar Cell Efficiency World Record of ...

items.description: In a dramatic one-two punch over the weekend, Chinese solar manufacturers Trina Solar and Longi both announced record-breaking silicon solar cell efficiencies above 28%, with each company's result independently certified by Germany's Institute for Solar Energy Research Hamelin (ISFH).

items.title: Colombia summit yields mandate for fossil fuel treaty talks

featured_image.name: The world's first fossil fuel phaseout conference has begun in Santa Marta,  Colombia, with 57 countries representing more than half of global GDP, 30%  of the world's population and 20% of global

items.description: Around 60 countries are meeting this week in the Colombian coastal city of Santa Marta for what organizers are calling the first global conference dedicated to transitioning away from fossil fuels — a gathering that pointedly excludes the world's largest greenhouse gas emitters, including the United States, China, and Russia.

items.title: India's power demand hits record as heatwave and Iran war strain global energy markets

featured_image.name: India's power grid creaks under hybrid work model, heatwave | Reuters

items.description: The Iran war and a punishing heatwave across South Asia are reshaping global energy markets in real time, driving record-breaking demand for Chinese clean technology exports, pushing India's power grid to its limits, and reinforcing Europe's pivot toward renewables.

items.title: BOJ holds rates but 6-3 split signals June hike

featured_image.name: Bank of Japan holds key rate as Middle East war dims outlook

items.description: The Bank of Japan held its benchmark interest rate at 0.75% on Tuesday in a 6-3 vote that revealed growing pressure within the central bank to tighten policy, kicking off a consequential week for global monetary policy with the Federal Reserve set to announce its own decision on Wednesday.

items.title: Iran war energy shock pushes millions back to charcoal and firewood

featured_image.name: DRC's reliance on charcoal threatens forests and fuels armed conflict

items.description: Two months after the start of the Iran war upended global energy markets, soaring fuel prices are forcing millions of families in Africa and South Asia to abandon cleaner cooking methods and revert to charcoal and firewood — a shift that conservationists warn is accelerating deforestation and threatening fragile wildlife habitats.

items.title: Iraq taps political newcomer al-Zaidi as prime minister-designate

featured_image.name: Iraq president nominates Ali al-Zaidi as PM-designate - Le Monde

items.description:
Iraqi President Nizar Amedi on Monday designated Ali al-Zaidi, a 40-year-old businessman and political newcomer, as prime minister-designate, tasking him with forming a new government after months of political deadlock and weeks of fraught negotiations shaped by American pressure.[1][2][3]

The appointment came on the final day of the constitutional deadline, after the Coordination Framework — a coalition of Shiite factions holding around 185 of parliament's 329 seats — endorsed al-Zaidi as its "consensus candidate" following a meeting at the government palace in Baghdad.[4][5]

items.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz, but Trump is dissatisfied with proposal

featured_image.name: Trump 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal to reopen Strait Hormuz,  end the war

items.description: Iran offered the United States a new proposal on Monday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the two-month-old war, but the plan — which would defer the core dispute over Tehran's nuclear program — drew a cool reception from President Trump and exposed divisions within his administration over how to proceed.

items.title: First LNG tanker crosses Hormuz since Iran war began

featured_image.name: ADNOC LNG Tanker Crosses Strait Of Hormuz - Marine Link

items.description:
A liquefied natural gas tanker managed by the UAE's ADNOC has crossed the Strait of Hormuz and appeared off the west coast of India, ship-tracking data showed on Monday, in what would be the first loaded LNG tanker to transit the strait since the Iran war began on February 28.[1][2]

The 136,357-cubic-meter vessel was last seen in the Gulf on March 30 before reappearing near India after several weeks without a signal, according to data from ICIS LNG Edge, Marine Traffic and LSEG. Ships in the Gulf have increasingly resorted to evasive tactics, including stopping location transmissions or broadcasting false identification numbers, to avoid being targeted or detained.[2]

items.title: Iran war and record heat reshape global energy markets

featured_image.name: Iranians hold talks with Europeans and U.N. Security Council : NPR

items.description: Two months into the war in Iran, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and a punishing wave of early-season heat across Asia are reshaping global energy markets, driving record electricity demand and accelerating a shift toward renewable power — with China emerging as the chief beneficiary.
